content: Isobutane, also referred to as methylpropane or 2-methylpropane, is a hydrocarbon classified as an alkane. It is an isomer of butane, meaning it shares the same molecular formula but has a different structural arrangement. Due to growing concerns about the depletion of the ozone layer caused by freon gases, isobutane has become increasingly utilized as a refrigerant gas, particularly in domestic refrigeration systems such as refrigerators and freezers. Additionally, it is widely employed as a propellant in aerosol sprays. When used in these capacities, isobutane is also designated as R-600a. In the petrochemical industry, isobutane serves as a feedstock for various chemical processes, including the synthesis of isooctane, a compound commonly used to enhance the octane rating of gasoline. The nomenclature of isobutane has been standardized by the International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry (IUPAC). In its 1993 recommendations for the nomenclature of organic chemistry, IUPAC retained isobutane as the trivial name for this compound. The systematic name for isobutane is methylpropane. The 2prefix in 2-methylpropane is considered unnecessary because there are no other isomers of this molecule that would require such differentiation in its name.
